newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN POLICE RETURN HUNGARIAN FLAG TO CONSULATE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN POLICE RETURN HUNGARIAN FLAG TO CONSULATE.

text.p: Romanian police resolved an embarrassing diplomatic incident on Saturday when they returned a stolen flag to the new Hungarian consulate in the city of Cluj.
The flag had been taken just two days after the consulate opened this week.
Police said three men had been arrested and face stiff jail terms if convicted.

The consulate, shut by Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu in 1988, was reopened by the two countries' foreign ministers on Wednesday to cheers from a crowd of several hundred. Many belonged to Romania 's 1.6 million strong Hungarian community.
But on Friday the Hungarian red, white and green flag was snatched from the building, triggering a big police operation.
A police spokesman said three city-hall employees had admitted the theft.
Cluj, 300 km (220 miles) northwest of Bucharest, is the stronghold of nationalist mayor Gheorghe Funar, who enraged ethnic Hungarians in the city by curbing their language rights.
He had opposed the reopening of the consulate and vowed to impose a law introduced by the former leftist government banning the display of foreign flags on private buildings.
Police said there was no political motive behind the theft.
